posts.title: Bluebirds for Garden Letters
posts.content:
Garden Letters wanted a spring cover that felt like the first warm Saturday. Two birds, lots of air, room for the masthead at the top.

Client

Garden Letters magazine

Used for

Spring issue cover

Year

2025

Medium

Gouache, finished digitally

The brief

Garden Letters wanted a spring cover that felt like the first warm Saturday. Two birds, lots of air, room for the masthead at the top.

What I did

Four pencil roughs, one colour study in blue and rust, then the final in gouache at A3. The magazine chose the second rough; I still prefer the fourth.

From rough to final

The cover sold out in the shops in nine days. People wrote in asking for the birds as a print, so we let Joon sell one.

Tomasz Nowak, art editor, Garden Letters

What happened next

The magazine printed 400 extra copies. The print is now the best seller in the shop, which I did not see coming.

Art direction

Tomasz Nowak

Print edition

A3, 150 copies

posts.title: Barred owl, cover for The Night Walk
posts.content:
Little Toller wanted a cover that worked at thumbnail size on a phone and full size on a table in a bookshop. The book is about walking at night, so: dark, but not gloomy.

Client

Little Toller Books

Used for

Hardback cover and endpapers

Year

2025

Medium

Gouache and pencil

The brief

Little Toller wanted a cover that worked at thumbnail size on a phone and full size on a table in a bookshop. The book is about walking at night, so: dark, but not gloomy.

What I did

Eleven roughs of the owl, one of the squirrel. The final is gouache on a mid-grey ground so the pale feathers do the work. The endpapers are the same branch, empty.

From rough to final

The best cover we have printed in years, and the only one people asked to buy.

Ellie Gray, Little Toller Books

What happened next

It went to a second printing in the first month. The owl is now an A3 print.

Designer

Ellie Gray

Format

Hardback, 216 pages

posts.title: Crow and blossom, tea tins for Kinoko
posts.excerpt: Tin wrap for a spring green tea, 2025
posts.content:
Kinoko Tea in Stokes Croft needed a tin wrap for a spring green tea. The tin is small and round, so the drawing had to work in a strip 7 cm tall.

Client

Kinoko Tea, Stokes Croft

Used for

Tin wrap for a spring green tea

Year

2025

Medium

Gouache on toned paper

The brief

Kinoko Tea in Stokes Croft needed a tin wrap for a spring green tea. The tin is small and round, so the drawing had to work in a strip 7 cm tall.

What I did

One crow, one branch, painted on toned paper so the blossom could be pure white gouache. The branch wraps all the way round so the tin has no front.

From rough to final

People buy the tin for the tin. We have started selling it empty.

Hana Mori, Kinoko Tea

What happened next

The second tin, for a roasted tea, is on my desk now.

Printed by

A tin maker in Leicester

Run

2,000 tins

posts.title: Totterdown from the air, a house map
posts.excerpt: A map of their street and the view from it, 2025
posts.content:
Priya and Sam were leaving Totterdown after eleven years and wanted their street, the view from their bedroom window and the walk to the pub on one sheet.

Client

Priya and Sam, private commission

Used for

A map of their street and the view from it

Year

2025

Medium

Pen, ink and watercolour, 50 x 70 cm

The brief

Priya and Sam were leaving Totterdown after eleven years and wanted their street, the view from their bedroom window and the walk to the pub on one sheet.

What I did

I walked it twice with a sketchbook, drew the plan in pencil at A2, then inked and painted it. Their cat is in the window of number 14. I didn't tell them.

From rough to final

The map is on our kitchen wall and we still find new things in it.

Priya and Sam

What happened next

They ordered two more prints for their parents. A neighbour on the same street asked for one of hers.

Size

50 x 70 cm

Time

Five weeks, with one round of changes

posts.title: Open studio dates for the year
posts.content:
The studio is open on the first Saturday of every month. The big one is Saturday 1 November, 11am to 4pm. I'll have the plan chest open, so you can look through roughs that never made it, and a box of seconds at £10 each.

Unit 4, Jamaica Street Studios. Two flights of stairs, no lift. If the stairs are a problem, email me and I'll bring things down to the courtyard.

posts.title: A page from the sketchbook
posts.content:
I keep one sketchbook for work and one for nothing in particular. This page is from the second one, drawn on a train to Cardiff while someone slept on my shoulder.

Neither page will ever be a print. That is what the second sketchbook is for.

posts.title: The owl is back in stock
posts.content: The barred owl A3 print sold out in a week in January. The reprint arrived on Tuesday: 100 copies on the same Hahnemuhle paper, checked one by one against the painting.
